source_text: Libido nihil attinet, inquit, ad semina, quia facta est a diabolo; huic autem libidini serviunt coniuges; semina autem et parvulos de seminibus facit Deus. Sed nec rei sunt, inquit, nec puniuntur parentes, qui agunt opus diaboli; sceleri autem et suppliciis destinantur parvuli, quos condidit Deus; impunitumque est quod fecit diabolus, id est libido; per quod docetur bona, quae nec supplicium meretur; sed accusatur damnaturque quod facit Deus; per quod docetur esse scelestum, quippe quod a supplicio, nec auctoris sui potest pudore defendi; credaturque hoc divinitas facere, quod nec extrema possit sustinere captivitas. Hunc habent exitum, qui inferunt veritati bellum, ut nihil non impium, non insanum loquantur; dum constet quia nulla oratione innocentium status ita, ut accusatorum suorum profanitate, defenditur.
pass_a_gloss: Lust pertains nothing, he says, to seeds, because it was made by the devil; but spouses serve this lust; but God makes seeds and little ones from seeds. But neither are the parents guilty, he says, nor are they punished, who do the devil's work; but little ones whom God founded are destined for crime and punishments; and what the devil made is unpunished, that is lust; through which it is taught good things, which do not even deserve punishment; but what God makes is accused and condemned; through which it is taught to be wicked, seeing that it cannot be defended from punishment even by the shame of its own author; and it is believed that divinity does this which not even extreme captivity could sustain. They have this end who bring war on truth, that they speak nothing not impious, not insane; while it stands that by no speech is the status of innocents so defended as by the profanity of their accusers.

lemmas.lexica: LS libido; Blaise pudenda libido vs nuptiae
LS parvulus; Blaise infants as Julian's test case

pass_b_english: Sexual desire, he says, has nothing to do with seed, because it was made by the devil. Married people serve this desire, while God makes seed and infants from seed. Yet the parents, who do the devil’s work, are neither guilty nor punished, he says. The infants whom God created, however, are assigned to crime and punishment. What the devil made—sexual desire—goes unpunished; it is thereby shown to be good, since it deserves no punishment. But what God makes is accused and condemned; it is thereby shown to be criminal, since not even respect for its maker can protect it from punishment. Divinity is to be believed to do something which even the most abject slavery could not endure. Such is the end of those who wage war on truth: they say nothing that is not impious and insane. Meanwhile, it is clear that no argument defends the innocent’s condition so well as the irreverence of their accusers does.
